bull.b: A 20-year, ~401 MW Anthropic lease (~$19B) provides durable, highly visible contracted revenue and long-term cash flow for buildouts. This materially de-risks demand, shifts mix toward contracted HPC leases versus spot mining, and underpins multi-year capacity planning and capital deployment.

~$3.0B cash/restricted cash and proceeds from the Abernathy JV sale strengthen funding for remaining project capex and near-term commitments. This liquidity supports completion of Lake Mariner and Muskie, lowers immediate refinancing pressure, and enables capital recycling into higher-return owned assets.

The Muskie acquisition and long-term utility agreements create a power-advantaged national platform able to scale to gigawatt levels. Secured grid access and potential integrated generation/storage at Morgantown support competitive cost of energy, a structural advantage in HPC/AI hosting markets.

bear.b: Stockholders' equity at zero in TTM and historically very high debt ratios indicate a fragile capitalization. This reduces financial flexibility, increases refinancing and covenant risk, and limits ability to absorb shocks or pursue opportunistic investments without dilutive or costly financing.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flows show core operations and buildouts are not self-funding. Persistent cash burn forces reliance on asset monetizations, debt or equity issuance, increasing dilution or leverage risk and constraining long-term investment flexibility if contracted revenue lags.

bear.t: Deep GAAP losses and near-term margin pressure
bear.b: Very large GAAP losses (noncash warrant revaluations) plus negative adjusted EBITDA and reported HPC margins (~28% vs ~85% target) create profit volatility and indicate operating scale-up and pre-revenue costs are depressing near-term margins, delaying self-sustaining profitability.
